source_snapshot.procedure: Create mdadm level [0|1|5] with four NVMe members, format/mount/copy/hash, fail/remove/re-add one member, wait for rebuild, recheck hash and tear down.
source_snapshot.criteria: Create, fault, remove, add and rebuild successfully with correct file hash and array state.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL proposes an invalid two-device RAID5 and omits the source failure/rebuild lifecycle.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: Requires RAID5 confirmation, valid member count, exact disposable targets, one-fault-only guards and full lifecycle.

old_problem: The RAID5 title coexisted with a generic level placeholder, while DeepSeek proposed an impossible two-device RAID5 and omitted the destructive degraded/rebuild coverage.
disposition_reason: The row title fixes level=5 and the Procedure explicitly supplies four members and /dev/md3, a valid RAID5 topology. Stable runtime identities replace volatile device names without changing coverage. The complete one-member degraded/rebuild, file-integrity and teardown phases remain mandatory under destructive authorization.
decision_basis: Directly read Compatibility row132 all18 XLSX cells and history2739.
Resolved the level placeholder from the RAID5 row identity and preserved all four source members.
Rejected invalid two-device automation and retained one-fault-only degraded/rebuild/hash/teardown coverage; no DUT action occurred.

test_case.test_name: Parameterized four-member mdadm RAID5 degraded, rebuild, integrity and teardown validation
test_case.purpose: Verify an approved disposable four-member NVMe mdadm RAID5 remains usable and hash-correct after one member is failed/removed, rebuilds after re-add, and tears down precisely.
required_package: Critical destructive authorization and proof members are non-boot, unmounted, non-swap, non-LVM, non-RAID and data-free
Approved mount path, 512 MiB file/hash, rebuild timeout/load/thermal limits
Exact one-member fault/re-add, OOB, abort and teardown/recovery plan
test_case.test_command: After stable-identity exclusions and approval, create /dev/md3 at level=5 with exactly four approved members, verify clean active state, mkfs/mount and copy/hash the 512 MiB file. Fail/remove exactly one mapped member, prove degraded availability and hash, re-add that member, monitor rebuild to clean, recheck hash, then unmount/stop and zero metadata only on the same four members.
test_case.expected_result: The four-member RAID5 reaches clean state, remains accessible and hash-correct with one missing member, shows real rebuild progress after re-add, returns clean with all members, and is dismantled without affecting other storage.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact four-member level=5 identity, one-member degraded service, observed rebuild progress/completion, matching file hashes before/during/after and targeted teardown. A two-device command or clean-only snapshot cannot pass.
safety_gate: Destructive approval precedes create, mkfs, fault and zero-superblock.
Protect OS/boot/EFI, mounted, swap, LVM/device-mapper, existing RAID, management and valuable-data devices by stable identity.
Only one member may be failed; a second fault while degraded/rebuilding is prohibited.
Abort on identity drift, unexpected signature/state, filesystem error, stalled rebuild, media/thermal/power/BMC fault or failed unmount; no automatic retry.
expected_evidence: Approval, four-member map and preflight exclusions
Exact level=5 create/detail and clean baseline
Re-add with timestamped rebuild progress, clean completion, post-hash and targeted teardown logs
test_case.recovery: On deviation, stop all new mutations, protect the remaining three members, preserve mdadm events/detail, hashes, health and logs, and require storage-owner recovery. Never fail another member or clear metadata while degraded, rebuilding or mounted.

source_conflict.reason: RAID5 row identity resolves level=5 and the four explicit members form a valid topology; DeepSeek's invalid two-member substitution is rejected.
